neighbours.label: an auxiliary or modal right after a character pronoun in narrative prose ('She had to', 'he could', 'He was'), a state or obligation rather than an action (the - pole fires on concrete actions: 'took', 'kisses')
fire: Rain was falling hard outside the window. She had to finish the letter before the post left.
"I never trusted him," Mara said. But he could not stay angry at his brother for long.
After the long march the soldier sat down by the fire. He was too tired to speak.
Tomas looked at the empty chair across the table. He would have to tell her soon.
The baker's daughter stared at the burnt loaves. She had to admit the oven was too hot.
When the train finally stopped, Elena gathered her bags. She could hardly believe she was home.
The old fisherman watched the storm clouds gather. He knew the boats must stay in port.
Lying awake at midnight, the boy listened to the wind. He was afraid of the dark attic.
quiet: Rain was falling hard outside the window. She folded the letter and walked to the post office.
"I never trusted him," Mara said. Then he slammed the door and left the house.
After the long march the soldier sat down by the fire. He pulled off his boots.
Tomas looked at the empty chair across the table. He poured himself more wine.
The baker's daughter stared at the burnt loaves. She threw them into the bin.
When the train finally stopped, Elena gathered her bags. She stepped onto the platform.
The old fisherman watched the storm clouds gather. He tied the boats to the pier.
Lying awake at midnight, the boy listened to the wind. He climbed out of bed.

notes: Card: ' could' x5, ' to' (had to) x4, ' was' x4, ' will' x3 in narrative. - pole peaks on action verbs (took, secretly told, kisses).
